question: Can a public-only policy choose an action from the complete native legal-action menu that never introduces a catastrophe against either frozen comparator (S0, Nexus-else-S0) while retaining material decision value?

definitions.publicInformation: STAGE3H_PUBLIC_DECISION_INFORMATION_V1 (complete public view incl. full public history; integrity digests excluded); no hidden node health/value, no seed recovery, no simulator/evaluator at decision time
definitions.actionIdentity: an action is identified by its identity-free semantic key: type, actor displacement/destination relative to the actor, the target entity's public attributes (kind, relative position, critical/objective/hostile/threatened/in-service/hub flags, observed relationships) and remaining non-identifier parameters; handles and entity ids are not part of it
definitions.relabelEquivalence: two actions are the same under entity relabelling iff their semantic keys are equal; verified per class by applying the O-2R.1 opaque relabelling to the public view

comparators.NEXUS: frozen Nexus recommendation, S0 on abstention (N); lexical tie-break unchanged

definitions.menu: the complete native legal-action menu = FORGE_ACTION_SURFACE_SYMMETRIC_V1 (policySurface), identical across a public-equivalence class
definitions.policyClass: pi: public decision information -> one menu action (deterministic) or a distribution over menu actions
definitions.introduction: runner-design potentialIntroduction({a}, comparator): a catastrophic while the comparator contains a non-catastrophic action
definitions.introductionFree: action a is introduction-free in world w iff it introduces against neither B nor N in w; a class admits a zero-introduction public policy (on its tested worlds) iff the intersection of introduction-free sets over the class is non-empty
definitions.regret: nreg = regret / menu utility spread; best-of gap = nreg(chosen) - min(nreg(B), nreg(N))
definitions.hiddenRisk: risk that varies across a public-equivalence class (because hidden node health/value vary) is hidden risk; risk constant across the class is publicly determined on the tested family

population.source: the 341 admissible-state equivalence classes of the safety-feasibility search (H2, Nexus applicable, N != B, S0 introducing vs N or both regrets in [40,160]); twin families rebuilt identically; spent DEV seeds only
population.bias: near-threshold and introduction classes only, i.e. where the two frozen arms are most likely to fail; classes far from the threshold were not analysed

verdictRule: B if any empty introduction-free intersection; else A if, over arm-failing classes, the offline minimax choice is >= 0.02 nreg below both frozen arms; else D
caveats: finite twin families sample the admissible hidden-state support; a non-empty intersection on tested worlds is not universal safety
the minimax choice is an offline, privileged in-class oracle; it is not a policy and not deployable
the analysed classes are a biased sample of hard cases
C (observability limit) remains open: whether lawful public features predict the introduction-free set can only be tested prospectively
